item.statement: Minima of cosine sums over Z_p / sets with small Fourier bias need Theta(log p) elements
item.what_to_check: Chowla cosine problem, epsilon-biased sets, Alon 2009 lower bounds; sidelobe design

chk.evidence:
Notes: /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/u6-cosine-sum-minima/CHECK.md.

Setup: with equal weights on K frequencies, m(y) = min_{delta!=0} sum_j y_j(1-cos(2 pi j delta/p)) equals K minus half the second eigenvalue of Cay(Z_p, {±j}). So the classical background is "abelian Cayley graphs need Omega(log n) generators to expand, and O(log n) random ones suffice."

Sources I fetched and read this session:

(1) Alon & Roichman, RSA 5(2):271-284, 1994. Metadata from Crossref; text from the author PDF web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/exp1.pdf.
- Abstract: "For Abelian groups this is essentially tight."
- Sec. 3, Proposition 3, verbatim: "For every fixed delta>0 there is a constant c=c(delta)>0 such that the following holds; If A is an Abelian group of order n, and X(A,S) is a delta-expander, then |S| >= c log_2 n."
- Prop. 7' gives a closed-walk lower bound on |mu_1| for arbitrary S. This is the same device as eq:posfourier.
- This entry is already in the bib (alon1994random), but the paper cites it only for the random lower bound. It is not cited for the Omega(log) necessity.

(2) Friedman, Murty & Tillich, JCTB 96(1):111-121, 2006. Metadata from Crossref; text from the author PDF at rocq.inria.fr.
- Abstract, verbatim: "a d-regular Cayley graph on an Abelian group of order n has second eigenvalue bounded below by d - O(dn^{-4/d}) ... for a large odd prime, n, the O(dn^{-4/d}) cannot be improved."
- Sec. 2, Thm 2 is the sphere-packing proof. Sec. 4, Thm 7 covers random Cayley graphs on Z/nZ with n prime.
- This is the quantitative unweighted form of our upper bound.

(3) Alon, "Perturbed identity matrices have high rank", CPC 18(1-2):3-15, 2009. Metadata from the Cambridge page; text from the author PDF identity1.pdf.
- Thm 7.1: an eps-biased family of n ±1 variables needs a sample space of size Omega(n/(eps^2 log(1/eps))).
- It is two-sided and stated only for Z_2^n, so it is adjacent at best.

Checked and rejected:
- Chowla cosine problem (Bedert arXiv 2509.05260, JMTZ arXiv 2509.03490, Shankar arXiv 2609.05338; from the sweep). It bounds how negative min sum cos must be, which is the opposite tail from ours. Neither result implies the other.
- Sidelobe and coding literature (AIKPS 1990 thin sets). Two-sided explicit constructions only; optional.
- Dirichlet / Bohr-set bound (Tao-Vu Lemma 4.20). Not fetched, so I give no bib entry.

What none of these covers: they are all unweighted, fixed-degree statements. I found no weighted concave-l_{1/s}-budget analogue. That analogue is the two-sided Theta((log p)^{1-s}), the Theta(log p) support with a share floor, and the o(log p) vanishing fraction. My web-search budget was exhausted, so this relies on the fetched PDFs and the sibling items t9, r25 and r26.

recommended_citations.why: Already in bib. Cite it in the thm:scaling discussion for the necessity half: Prop. 3 says an abelian Cayley graph that is a delta-expander needs |S| >= c(delta) log2 n. Thm 2 covers sufficiency for random sets. Together they are the unweighted Theta(log p) statement.

The quantitative unweighted version of the upper bound on m(y): lambda_2 >= d - O(d n^{-4/d}) for d-regular abelian Cayley graphs, tight for prime n. With equal shares this gives m = O(K p^{-2/K}), so K must be Omega(log p).

Optional 'cf.' citation. Thm 7.1 is the two-sided small-bias lower bound: an eps-biased family of n variables needs a sample space of size Omega(n/(eps^2 log 1/eps)), i.e. eps-biased sets in Z_2^n have size Omega(log|G|). It is stated for Z_2^n only and is two-sided, so it is weaker than what the paper needs.

chk.recommended_change:
In cyclic.tex, after the paragraph following thm:scaling (or after cor:few), add:

"With equal shares, $m(y)$ is $K$ minus half the second eigenvalue of $\mathrm{Cay}(\sZ_p,\{\pm j\})$. So the unweighted case of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling} is the classical fact that Cayley graphs of abelian groups need $\Omega(\log n)$ generators to expand, while $O(\log n)$ random ones suffice \citep[Thm.~2, Prop.~3]{alon1994random}. Quantitatively, $\lambda_2\ge d-O(dn^{-4/d})$, which is tight for prime $n$ \citep{friedman2006spectral}. Our contribution is the weighted version under the concave budget $\sum_j y_j^{1/s}\le1$, where pigeonhole alone gives only $K=O(\log p/\log\log p)$. Unlike Chowla's cosine problem, which asks how negative a cosine sum must become, this concerns how close to its peak it must return."

Also add the friedman2006spectral bib entry. Do not cite the Chowla papers as support.
